title: Spending Limits Carried by Each of the Mountain Dining Plans
content:
Two limits stand over what may be taken off a Mountain Dining Plans card: the largest amount that may be spent on the plan in one calendar day, and the largest amount that may be spent in one transaction. A third column records whether someone other than the named holder may spend the plan at all.

| Plan | Largest in one calendar day | Largest in one transaction | Spending by someone other than the named holder |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mountain Bites Dining Card | $150.00 | $75.00 | not allowed |
| Peak Plate Dining Plan | $300.00 | $150.00 | not allowed |
| Summit Table Dining Plan | $600.00 | $350.00 | allowed |
| Alpine Club Dining Membership | $1500.00 | $900.00 | allowed |
| Chef's Table Dining Membership | $3500.00 | $2500.00 | allowed |
| Collective Hospitality Dining Membership | $9000.00 | $6000.00 | allowed |

The two limits answer different questions and the smaller of them is always the per-transaction figure. On the Peak Plate Dining Plan, for instance, the day's limit of $300.00 is twice the transaction limit of $150.00, so that plan's day may hold two transactions at the full transaction limit and no more; on the Chef's Table Dining Membership the day's limit of $3500.00 stands above the transaction limit of $2500.00 by $1000.00, so a second transaction on the same day may run only to that remainder.
